title: SpaceXAI backs Omarchy with $1.5M in Grok tokens
content:
SpaceXAI has announced it is joining the Omacom Foundation, the organization overseeing the Linux distribution Omarchy, as a Founding Corporate Patron. As part of this partnership, SpaceXAI will donate $1.5 million worth of Grok tokens to the project. David Heinemeier Hansson, the Danish entrepreneur who created Ruby on Rails and co-founded the company behind Basecamp, leads the Omarchy initiative.

According to a blog post by Hansson, the donated tokens will be primarily utilized to accelerate development, review code, and patch bugs within the Linux distribution. The announcement highlights the collaboration between the AI-focused entity and the controversial open-source project.
summary: SpaceXAI announced it would join the Omacom Foundation as a Founding Corporate Patron and donate $1.5 million worth of Grok tokens to Omarchy, a Linux project led by David Heinemeier Hansson. The tokens will be used to accelerate development, review code, and patch bugs.
author: The Verge

title: USA Today sues OpenAI over alleged unauthorized use of articles
content:
USA Today Co. and several of its local newspapers have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the tech company copied "hundreds of thousands" of articles to train its AI models. In the filing submitted on Thursday, the publisher is seeking damages exceeding $250 million, claiming that OpenAI’s unauthorized use of its content has caused "real and continuing" harm to its outlets.

This legal action is the latest in a series of copyright lawsuits against OpenAI. The company is also currently facing legal proceedings from The New York Times, The Intercept, CNET owner Ziff Davis, CBC/Radio-Canada, and Encyclopaedia.
summary: USA Today Co. and its local newspapers are suing OpenAI for allegedly copying hundreds of thousands of articles to train its AI models. The publisher is seeking more than $250 million in damages, claiming the unauthorized use caused real and continuing harm to its outlets.
author: The Verge

title: Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Release Delayed to January 26, 2027
content:
Playground Games has officially delayed the PlayStation 5 release of Forza Horizon 6 to January 26, 2027. This pushback follows an earlier announcement that the game would arrive on the platform in 2026, with the new date aligning the console launch with the release of a new game expansion.

The PS5 version will coincide with the expansion, which will also be available on Xbox and PC in January. The game originally debuted on Xbox and PC on May 15. Additionally, Playground Games will offer a Premium Edition for PS5 that provides up to five days of early access prior to the official launch date.
summary: Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 is delayed to January 26, 2027, from its originally planned 2026 release. The PS5 version will launch with a Premium Edition offering up to five days of early access, and a new expansion will also be released on Xbox and PC in January.
author: The Verge

title: Pokémon Legends: Z‑A Still on Sale After Amazon Prime Day
content:
Amazon Prime Day has ended, but the Pokémon Legends: Z‑A deal remains active.  The title is available on Amazon for $39.88, down from its usual $59.99 for the Nintendo Switch and $69.99 for the Switch 2.

Pokémon Legends: Z‑A is the first main‑series entry to replace the traditional turn‑based system with real‑time battles.  Players still catch, level up, trade, and battle Pokémon in a Paris‑inspired setting that features the game’s unique Lumiose City.  The Switch 2 version is noted for its smooth performance.

The game’s “Mega Dimension” DLC is available as a paid add‑on for $29.99.  A bundled Switch 2 Edition that includes the base game and the DLC will be released on October 29th, 2026 for $99.99, so the current discount offers a cheaper option.
summary: Pokémon Legends: Z‑A is still available on Amazon at $39.88 after the Prime Day sale. The game is the first in the main series to use a real‑time battling system instead of the traditional turn‑based formula.
author: The Verge

title: Tim Cook says he is not meddling in new Apple CEO John Ternus's work
content:
Tim Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive officer in September, handing the top job to former hardware chief John Ternus and taking on an executive chairman role.  

Cook remains a visible representative of the company, having been photographed attending a state dinner at the White House.  

In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he is “not meddling” in Ternus’ work. He emphasized the “incredible level of trust” between them and the need for frequent, significant communication, adding that his current focus is on worldwide policy.
summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in September and became executive chairman, handing the top job to former hardware chief John Ternus. In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he is not meddling in Ternus' work and is focusing on worldwide policy.
author: The Verge

title: Paramount to adapt Cyberpunk 2077 into live‑action film
content:
Paramount Pictures has announced that it is developing a live‑action film based on CD Projekt Red’s video‑game franchise Cyberpunk 2077. The project has no release date yet, but Deadline reports that Lorenzo di Bonaventura—known for producing the Transformers films—will serve as a producer.

Cyberpunk 2077, which launched in 2020, has become a major commercial success, with CD Projekt Red reporting more than 40 million copies sold. The franchise has also been adapted into a hit Netflix anime.
summary: Paramount Pictures is producing a live‑action film adaptation of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, with Lorenzo di Bonaventura as producer. No release date has been announced yet.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft Releases Faster Windows 11 Search in Testing
content:
Microsoft is addressing long‑standing frustration with Windows Search in Windows 11 by launching a significant redesign. The new search experience is currently in testing and is described as faster, more capable, and more modern than its predecessor.

Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team, said the updated search is “built for speed” and is built on WinUI 3 as part of a broader investment in modernizing core Windows experiences.

Early testing has shown substantial improvements in performance and memory usage. The Verge reports these details.
summary: Microsoft is testing a redesigned Windows Search for Windows 11 that is faster and more modern. Early tests show substantial improvements in performance and memory usage, according to Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon builds 1,000th satellite, plans space internet launch by year end
content:
Amazon has built its 1,000th satellite and plans to launch its space‑internet service by the end of the year.

In a statement, Amazon noted, “If this was easy, everybody else would be doing it.”

The company is preparing for the year‑end launch of its space‑internet service.
summary: Amazon has built its 1,000th satellite. The company plans to launch a space internet service by the end of the year.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon's Alexa Tablets Drop Fire Branding, Switch to Google Play
content:
Amazon has released new Alexa‑powered tablets that no longer carry the Fire branding, signaling a shift toward a more Android‑centric experience.  

According to the company’s announcement, Amazon has removed its own app store from the devices, making Google Play the primary source for applications.
summary: Amazon's new Alexa Tablets no longer carry the Fire branding. Amazon has removed its app store, so the tablets use Google Play.
author: Ars Technica

title: Former Stratton Oakmont partner launches AI startup for ex‑cons
content:
Richard Bronson, a former Stratton Oakmont partner who served time in federal prison for securities violations, has launched a new startup called Commissary Club. The company aims to serve an untapped market: people leaving prison.

Commissary Club uses artificial intelligence to help ex‑prisoners find jobs, secure housing, connect with community resources, and even arrange dates. The platform is designed to support individuals in their transition back into society.
summary: Richard Bronson, a former Stratton Oakmont partner who served federal prison time for securities violations, has launched Commissary Club. The AI‑driven startup aims to help people leaving prison find jobs, housing, community and dates.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI's math proofs deviate from researchers' guidelines, falling short of standards
content:
OpenAI’s recent output of mathematical proofs has been found to fall short of the standards expected by the discipline.  

According to the source, the company’s “flood of proofs” deviated from guidelines established by a group of mathematical researchers that OpenAI consulted. The divergence suggests that the lab’s current approach does not align with the criteria set by the experts.  

The discrepancy highlights a gap between OpenAI’s generated solutions and the field’s established expectations.
summary: OpenAI’s math solutions aren’t meeting the field’s standards yet. OpenAI's flood of proofs deviated from the guidelines set by a group of mathematical researchers consulted by the frontier lab.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Updates Usage Policy to Ban Model Abuse and Election Interference
content:
Anthropic has revised its usage policy, adding new restrictions on how its Claude models may be used. The updated rules explicitly ban repeated abuse of the model in extreme cases, while still permitting ordinary frustration and criticism.

The policy also expands to cover broader concerns, including election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance. Anthropic’s changes aim to prevent misuse of its AI technology in these areas.
summary: Anthropic's updated usage policy prohibits users from repeatedly abusing Claude in extreme cases. The new rules also cover election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google turns Gemini into agentic AI for businesses
content:
Google is transforming its Gemini platform into an AI agent capable of planning and executing tasks across various business applications and systems. This new functionality allows the agent to manage complex workflows by delegating specific responsibilities to subagents and utilizing multiple AI models simultaneously.

To integrate more deeply into professional environments, the Gemini agent is assigned its own workplace identity, which includes a dedicated email address. This setup enables the AI to communicate and operate within existing business infrastructure as an autonomous entity.
summary: Google is transforming Gemini into an AI agent that plans and executes tasks across business apps. The agent can delegate work to subagents, use multiple models, and has its own workplace identity with an email address.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI revenue reported $20B lower than earlier estimate
content:
OpenAI’s revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected.

Earlier reports had estimated the AI lab’s annualized revenue at about $70 billion. A new report now claims the figure is significantly lower, indicating a substantial shortfall from the earlier projection.
summary: Earlier reports said OpenAI’s annualized revenue was about $70 billion. A new report claims it is a whole lot less than that.
author: TechCrunch

title: Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months
content:
The company behind the popular LMArena leaderboard has seen its valuation nearly double to $3.1 billion within ten months.  

In a recent funding round, the firm raised $200 million, led by Lightspeed and Khosla.  

The company is now expanding its focus to measure AI models on alignment issues, including the tendency to lie.
summary: The company behind the popular LMArena leaderboard has raised $200 million led by Lightspeed and Khosla, and is now measuring AI models on alignment issues such as lying.
author: TechCrunch

title: Ben Affleck Goes Viral for AI Expertise After Selling Startup to Netflix
content:
Ben Affleck is going viral for his deep knowledge of AI.  

The actor has demonstrated expertise in neural networks, transformers, and open weights.  

Affleck sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year.  

He is proving he is more than just a Hollywood star.
summary: Ben Affleck is going viral for his deep knowledge of AI, from neural networks and transformers to open weights. The actor sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year.
author: TechCrunch

title: Baku experts call for action amid global missing persons surge
content:
Experts in Baku urged action as the number of missing persons surges worldwide and in Ukraine.  

Around 280,000 people are registered as missing in Ukraine alone, with 10,000 new cases added each month. This figure is part of a 70 % global rise in missing-person cases since 2019.  

Forensic experts meeting in Baku said the obstacle to resolving these cases is not a lack of forensic capacity but governmental reluctance.
summary: Around 280,000 people are registered as missing in Ukraine alone, with 10,000 new cases added each month, part of a 70% global rise since 2019. Forensic experts meeting in Baku said the obstacle was not forensic capacity but governmental reluctance.
author: Euronews

title: Heavy autumn snow paralyses roads in Russia's Magadan region, disrupting trucks and buses
content:
Heavy autumn snowfall has paralysed roads in Russia’s Magadan region, part of the Far East. The sudden accumulation of snow has made driving conditions extremely difficult for vehicles on the area’s highways.

Trucks are struggling to navigate through the deep snow, and intercity bus services have been disrupted. The severe weather has halted regular traffic flow and caused significant delays for freight and passenger transport.

The snowfall has caused significant transportation disruptions in the region.
summary: Heavy autumn snowfall has paralysed roads in Russia’s Magadan region. The conditions have left trucks struggling through snow and have disrupted intercity bus services.
author: Euronews

title: US charges ex-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro with torture
content:
The United States has formally charged former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture.  

The revised indictment notes multiple references to the participation of Venezuela’s DGCIM military intelligence agency, described as a feared entity.  

The document underscores the agency’s alleged involvement in the alleged crimes.
summary: The United States has charged former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro with torture. The revised indictment cites involvement of Venezuela’s DGCIM military intelligence agency.
author: Euronews

title: Hashtag #IAmJaneDoe spreads on social media in solidarity with Cornell assault victim
content:
A wave of videos is circulating on social media under the hashtag #IAmJaneDoe, signaling public solidarity with an anonymous Cornell University student. The student alleges she was sexually assaulted in 2024 by several members of a fraternity.

The online campaign uses the hashtag to amplify the victim’s claim and to draw attention to the alleged assault. No further details about the incident or the participants have been provided.
summary: A wave of videos is spreading across social media under the hashtag #IAmJaneDoe. The videos express solidarity with an anonymous Cornell University student who alleges she was sexually assaulted by several fraternity members in 2024.
author: France 24

title: SpaceX returns Sophie Adenot and crew after eight‑month ISS mission
content:
SpaceX returned four astronauts to Earth on Thursday after they completed an eight‑month stay aboard the International Space Station. The crew included France’s Sophie Adenot, U.S. astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, and Russia’s Andrey Fedyaev.

During the mission, Adenot became the first French woman to walk in space, marking a historic milestone for France’s space program. The eight‑month expedition concluded with the successful splashdown of the SpaceX vehicle.
summary: SpaceX brought France's Sophie Adenot and fellow astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway and Andrey Fedyaev back to Earth on Thursday. The four completed an eight‑month mission aboard the International Space Station, during which Adenot became the first French woman to walk in space.
author: France 24

title: Two Latvian men arrested near RAF base in southeast England housing US and NATO intelligence
content:
British counter‑terrorism police announced Thursday that two Latvian men were arrested near a Royal Air Force base in southeast England that hosts United States and NATO intelligence operations, according to a police statement.

The arrests follow a major incident at a different UK base that prompted the United States military to withdraw B‑1 bombers stationed there.
summary: British counter‑terrorism police are investigating after two Latvian men were arrested Thursday near a Royal Air Force base in southeast England that houses US and NATO intelligence operations. The arrests came days after a major incident at another UK base led the US military to withdraw B‑1 bombers stationed there.
author: France 24

title: French parties' responses to student protests examined as elections approach
content:
Students across France have vowed to continue street demonstrations even after the prime minister addressed the issue in a Wednesday speech, promising that the government would devise a plan to meet their concerns.

The response of France’s political parties to the ongoing student movement is being examined by reporter Delano D’Souza.
summary: Students in France say they will continue street protests even after the prime minister said the government will devise a plan to address their concerns. Reporter Delano D'Souza is examining how French political parties are reacting to the movement.
author: France 24

title: Residents of Oleshky face starvation under Russian occupation
content:
Residents of Oleshky, a town in southern Ukraine now under Russian occupation, are facing starvation.  The community, located near the Ukrainian city of Kherson on the war’s southern front, has been under Russian control since 2022.

With food deliveries halted since May, residents and refugees are forced to travel for hours on foot or by bicycle along roads littered with mines to obtain food and water.  Former residents and Ukrainian refugees are now attempting to raise awareness of the crisis.
summary: Residents of the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine are traveling on foot and bicycle for hours over mine‑strewn roads to obtain food and water. Food deliveries have stopped since May, prompting former residents and Ukrainian refugees to raise the alarm.
author: France 24

title: Russian strike on Kramatorsk buses kills 30, Zelensky vows response
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday that Ukraine would respond to a Russian strike that hit two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, killing 30 people and wounding 18 others.  

France 24 reporter Andrew Hilliar described the attack as part of a growing number of Russian assaults on civilians, noting UN figures that show more civilians had been killed in Ukraine as of August this year than in all of 2025.  

The incident underscores what officials describe as a steady increase in attacks on civilians in the conflict.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday there would be a response to a Russian strike that hit two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, killing 30 people and wounding 18 others. France 24's Andrew Hilliar said the attack is part of a growing number of Russian attacks on civilians, with UN figures showing more civilians had been killed in Ukraine as of August this year than in all of 2025.
author: France 24

title: Aaron Sorkin's new film "The Social Reckoning" stars Mikey Madison and Jeremy Allen White
content:
Aaron Sorkin returns to the subject of Facebook fifteen years after directing “The Social Network” with a new film titled “The Social Reckoning.” The project examines the platform’s influence on division, extremism and misinformation in America, issues that have fueled Sorkin’s long‑running public feud with Mark Zuckerberg.

“The Social Reckoning” dramatizes the true story of Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen, portrayed by Oscar‑nominated actress Mikey Madison (“Anora”). In the film, Haugen leaks thousands of internal documents to Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, a role played by Jeremy Allen White (“The Bear”).
summary: Aaron Sorkin is directing the new film "The Social Reckoning", which revisits Facebook fifteen years after "The Social Network". The movie dramatizes whistleblower Frances Haugen, portrayed by Mikey Madison, and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, portrayed by Jeremy Allen White.
author: France 24

title: India experiences water and power shortages due to weak monsoon
content:
India is confronting water and power shortages after a weak monsoon season. The deficient rainfall is affecting farmers, reducing water supplies and straining the power system.

The situation has also prompted broader concerns about increasingly erratic rainfall patterns and the associated economic costs.
summary: A weak monsoon in India is affecting farmers, water supplies and the power system. The situation is prompting questions about increasingly erratic rainfall and its economic costs.
author: DW World

title: Houthi‑Saudi conflict impacts African Red Sea coast near Bab el‑Mandeb
content:
The ongoing Houthi‑Saudi conflict is having a direct impact on countries along Africa’s Red Sea coast, according to recent reports.  

The Bab el‑Mandeb Strait, which Yemeni government forces are attempting to retake from the Houthis, lies close to Djibouti and other African states.
summary: The Bab el‑Mandeb Strait, located close to Djibouti and other African states, is part of the conflict. Yemeni government forces are trying to retake the strait from the Houthis.
author: DW World

title: EU, Canada and Lithuania withdraw support from Disinfo2026 event in Vilnius
content:
The EU’s diplomatic service, Canada, and the host nation of Lithuania have all withdrawn support for the Disinfo2026 event in Vilnius. The decision follows reports of U.S. pressure on the conference.

The EU said it was “uncomfortable with the framing” of some panels at the disinformation event.
summary: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. The EU said it was uncomfortable with the framing of some panels, amid reports of US pressure.
author: DW World

title: UNDP report: Conflict and climate shocks cause collapse of services for millions in Myanmar
content:
Myanmar’s poverty is worsening as families confront a cascade of hardships, according to a United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report released Thursday. The report links the deepening crisis to years of conflict, displacement, economic disruption and climate shocks across the country.

UNDP says these combined pressures have caused a “simultaneous collapse” of shelter, healthcare, schooling and livelihoods, affecting millions of people in Myanmar.
summary: Years of conflict, displacement, economic disruption and climate shocks in Myanmar have caused a “simultaneous collapse” of shelter, healthcare, schooling and livelihoods. The UN Development Programme said the collapse is affecting millions of people in a report issued on Thursday.
author: UN News

title: Afghan women face new dress code arrests as record refugee returns
content:
Afghan women and girls are facing new arrests over dress‑code violations, the United Nations said on Thursday. The UN warned that Taliban authorities are detaining and threatening further arrests of women and girls for alleged breaches of the regime’s clothing rules.

The warning comes as record numbers of Afghan refugees are returning home and trying to rebuild their lives. The surge in returnees coincides with the heightened enforcement of dress‑code restrictions, adding to the challenges faced by women and girls in the country.
summary: Afghan women and girls are being arrested, detained and threatened with arrest by Taliban authorities. The UN warned on Thursday that the arrests are occurring as record numbers of returnees struggle to rebuild their lives back home.
author: UN News

title: UN independent human rights expert warns age must not diminish rights of older women
content:
A United Nations independent human rights expert warned on Thursday that “age must never diminish rights,” highlighting the plight of older women worldwide.  

The expert said older women face violence, exploitation and neglect, yet remain largely invisible in the laws, policies, data and services designed to protect women overall.
summary: Older women around the world face violence, exploitation and neglect. A UN independent human rights expert said on Thursday they remain largely invisible in the laws, policies, data and services designed to protect women overall, warning that age must never diminish rights.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief: Legacy of slavery and colonialism is still fuelling racism
content:
UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday that the legacy of enslavement and colonialism continues to shape the lives of Africans and people of African descent.  

Türk called for urgent action to deliver reparatory justice that goes beyond financial compensation.
summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday that the legacy of enslavement and colonialism continues to shape the lives of Africans and people of African descent. He called for urgent action to deliver reparatory justice beyond financial compensation.
author: UN News

title: Nicolás Maduro and wife Cilia Flores indicted for alleged torture conspiracy
content:
The deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted on charges of alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed on Thursday.

The superseding indictment was released shortly before Flores appeared in court seeking pre‑trial release, a request that Judge Alvin Hellerstein denied. Both Maduro and Flores have remained in custody in New York City since early January.
summary: A superseding indictment unsealed Thursday in Manhattan federal court charged deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiracy to commit torture. Both have been jailed in New York City since early January, and Judge Alvin Hellerstein denied Flores’s request for pre‑trial release.
author: Guardian World

title: Ethiopian government drones strike Eritrean troops in Tigray after border incursion
content:
Ethiopian government forces launched a drone strike against Eritrean troops that had entered the Tigray region, civilian witnesses, a militia commander and the conflict‑monitoring group ACLED said. The Eritrean military vehicles crossed the southern border of Eritrea into Tigray on Wednesday and reached the town of Adigrat, about 25 miles (40 km) south of the border.

The drone attack raises concerns that renewed fighting inside Ethiopia could expand into a broader regional war involving the neighboring countries. No further details on casualties or damage were provided.
summary: Eritrean troops entered Ethiopia's Tigray region, driving military vehicles across the southern border and reaching the town of Adigrat. Ethiopian government forces responded with a drone attack on the Eritrean troops, prompting concerns of an expanded internal and regional war.
author: Guardian World

title: Aldabra giant tortoise population in Seychelles reaches 180,000
content:
A survey of the world’s largest free‑roaming giant tortoise population shows the Aldabra giant tortoise on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles has reached a record 180,000 individuals. The count reflects the success of a decades‑long recovery programme that has helped the once endangered species thrive.

The free‑roaming population now thrives on the Indian Ocean atoll, marking a significant conservation triumph for the species.
summary: A survey found the world’s largest free‑roaming giant tortoise population on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles has reached a record 180,000 individuals. The increase is attributed to a decades‑long recovery programme that has helped the once endangered species thrive.
author: Guardian World

title: Syria demands independent investigation of Black Sea ship sinking
content:
Syria has demanded an independent investigation into the sinking of a vessel in the Black Sea. Syrian officials said they were seeking answers about the incident.

The authorities also questioned why search and rescue operations were terminated before the fate of ten sailors aboard the ship could be determined.
summary: Syrian authorities called for an independent probe into the sinking of a ship in the Black Sea. They questioned why search and rescue operations were halted before the fate of ten sailors was known.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two Latvian men arrested after breach of RAF Molesworth base
content:
Two Latvian men were arrested after breaching the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a United Kingdom military airfield.  

Police have indicated that, to date, there is no evidence connecting the Molesworth incident to the events that took place at RAF Fairford last month.  

The investigation continues under the jurisdiction of local authorities.
summary: Two Latvian men were arrested after breaching the RAF Molesworth military base in the United Kingdom. Police said there is no indication the incident is linked to events at RAF Fairford last month.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Colombia to open embassy in Jerusalem, Israeli foreign minister reports
content:
Israeli Foreign Minister announced that Colombia will open an embassy in Jerusalem. The statement follows President Abelardo De la Espriella’s campaign pledge to deepen relations with Israel.  

De la Espriella had promised closer ties with Israel while campaigning, a promise now reflected in the planned diplomatic mission.
summary: Israeli foreign minister said Colombia will open an embassy in Jerusalem. President Abelardo De la Espriella had promised closer ties with Israel on the campaign trail.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel opens first national pavilion at Morocco's Marrakech Air Show
content:
Israel inaugurated its first national pavilion at the Marrakech Air Show in Morocco, marking the country's debut presence at the North African defence exhibition.  

The pavilion was attended by Israel’s leading military contractors, who joined the launch alongside officials at the event.
summary: Israel opened its first national pavilion at Morocco's Marrakech Air Show. The pavilion was joined by Israel's top military contractors.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ICC finds Philippines ex‑President Duterte fit to stand trial
content:
The International Criminal Court ruled that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte is fit to stand trial.  

A panel of experts concluded that the former president is able to understand the charges against him and can follow the court proceedings.  

The ICC’s determination affirms that Duterte meets the legal standards required to participate in a trial.
summary: The International Criminal Court ruled that former Philippine President Duterte is fit to stand trial. A panel of experts concluded he can understand the charges and follow the proceedings.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Man City manager Maresca says players unfazed by breaches verdict ahead of Liverpool
content: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said his players remain focused on the upcoming test against Liverpool despite a recent verdict on the club’s financial breaches. Maresca claimed the squad is unfazed by the ruling and is concentrating on the Liverpool showdown.
summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says his players are unfazed by the financial breaches verdict. He added they remain focused on the upcoming Liverpool test.
author: Al Jazeera

title: HRW says US deported over 500 migrants to Africa unlawfully
content: Human Rights Watch says that more than 500 migrants have been expelled from the United States to African countries, citing U.S. data. The organization characterizes the deportations as unlawful and as exploiting the migrants’ suffering. HRW’s statement underscores concerns about the legality and humanitarian impact of the removals. The group’s assessment is based on the reported figures and its analysis of the deportation practices.
summary: HRW says more than 500 migrants have been expelled from the United States to African countries. HRW says the deportations are unlawful and exploit suffering.
author: BBC World

title: Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture of US citizens
content:
Venezuela’s former president Nicolás Maduro has been charged with conspiracy to commit torture.  

The new accusations allege that, while Maduro was in power, U.S. citizens held in Venezuela were subjected to torture.  

The charges focus specifically on the alleged mistreatment of those U.S. detainees during his administration.
summary: Nicolás Maduro, ex-leader of Venezuela, has been charged with conspiracy to commit torture. The accusations involve alleged torture of U.S. citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.
author: BBC World

title: Below review – a killer snot-berg causes chaos for Josh Hartnett
content:
The six-part supernatural thriller Below centers on Snook’s Arm, a struggling fishing community in Newfoundland threatened by an ancient evil and a sudden, inexplicable iceberg. The series features Josh Hartnett as Calvin Penney, a father figure who reacts with shock to the massive CGI structure that materializes in the harbor, bringing further trouble to the embattled group of fishermen.

The narrative includes Wade Penney, portrayed by Charlie Heaton, who serves as a young roustabout and Airbnb host. Wade provides exposition about the local dangers, citing a 1986 tragedy in which his family’s cottage and his muscular grandfather were dragged underwater by unknown forces. The show also addresses broader challenges facing the town, including fishing bans, decades of economic uncertainty, and a looming government-led resettlement program.

Set against a backdrop of plaid shirts, sea hags, and 1970s-1990s nostalgia, the series is described as a ridiculous yet fun supernatural thriller. The production incorporates elements such as mist, motorbikes, curses, and the music of the Waterboys, while focusing on the community's battle against the supernatural menace.
summary: Don your best plaid shirts for this supernatural thriller about a gang of beefy fishermen who tackle sea monsters. It is totally ridiculous – but you will have loads of daft funAbandon all hope, ye who enter Below.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Ali G: Who Iz I? challenges character comedy's future in 2026
content:
Sacha Baron Cohen’s new film, Ali G: Who Iz I?, returns the comedian to the character that established his niche in gonzo-gotcha comedy during the late 1990s. The article questions whether the "big dog of Da West Staines Massiv" remains effective in the reality of 2026, noting that the satirical project originally targeted 1990s multicultural mores. It remains unclear if the character has stayed sufficiently relevant in a more rancorous era, particularly for real-life situations that previously featured interactions with figures like Donald Trump.

The release of the film places the future of character-led comedy on the line, as Baron Cohen appears to be the last remaining practitioner of this specific tradition in cinemas. The text defines character comedy not merely as comedy with characters, but as work filtered through a central persona whose subversive sensibility overlaps with the comedian and colors the entire production.
summary: Sacha Baron Cohen's new film Ali G: Who Iz I? revives his 1990s character to test if personality-driven comedy remains relevant in a more rancorous era. The article questions whether the satirical project can restore the genre to big screens or mark its end.
author: Guardian Culture

title: The Avalanches create new album and film with Haley Joel Osment
content:
Robbie Chater and Tony Di Blasi, the core members of the Australian disco-pop group the Avalanches, recently traveled to the mountainous region of Minakami, Japan, with actor Haley Joel Osment. The trio is working on a new album titled No Bad Memories, which will be accompanied by a 35-minute film. Osment, known for his roles in The Sixth Sense and Forrest Gump, joined the project after the band members noticed he frequently liked their Instagram posts and decided to reach out to him.

content:

In the conversation, Coppola discussed the influence of her mother on her filmmaking style, noting that she learned to be true to herself and to find beauty in odd details of life. She credited her mother for helping her capture the specific experience of being a young girl, a theme that resonated with an aspiring 14-year-old filmmaker who initiated the dialogue.

Coppola also addressed a question regarding the isolation of hotel rooms in her films, which are often detached from a character’s past or future. When asked to choose a cherished memory to preserve, she cited a recent party held at Versailles for the anniversary of Marie Antoinette. She described the moment when New Order began playing “Ceremony” and the lights turned on as a happy memory she knows she will remember in the future. Coppola added that she would not erase any painful memories, as she believes they are part of making a person who they are.

title: How the Kop’s chants propelled Andy Burnham to fight for Hillsborough justice
content:

Visitors from as far away as Australia had been laying flowers and messages beneath the stadium’s Eternal Flame since dawn. As the families walked from the Centenary Stand to their seats at the front of the Kop, the crowd stood to offer a loud and heartfelt ovation, reflecting raw anger over two decades of perceived lack of admission of guilt from authorities.

This atmosphere of heightened emotion preceded a speech at Anfield that was initially met with boos. The reaction to the address contributed to a change in approach by the Labour government, ultimately leading to an apology from David Cameron.

content:
Khaldoon al-Mubarak, chairman of Manchester City, is described as a key figure in the project to establish Abu Dhabi as a secure world power and the dominant member of the United Arab Emirates. The article suggests that his next major move may involve the sale of the club. Al-Mubarak’s deep ties to the emirate’s leadership stem from his family’s prominent role in the UAE’s founding and legal history.

His paternal grandfather, Ahmad Bin Abdul Aziz al-Mubarak, served as chair of Abu Dhabi’s Sharia judicial department and as a senior adviser to Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan al-Nahyan, the founding president of the UAE. In this capacity, Ahmad Bin Abdul Aziz helped craft the Islamic legal framework of the new nation during the 1970s.

title: Jonathan Liew questions if Fury v Joshua is merit or algorithmic celebrity power
content:
The upcoming fight between Fury and Joshua is described as occurring at the intersection of commercial potential and a lack of genuine competitive risk. Jonathan Liew poses the question of whether the event represents meritocratic sporting excellence or merely algorithmic celebrity power.

To illustrate the context of the discussion, the article references the 1912 Olympic marathon, which was held during a severe Scandinavian heatwave. Japanese runner Shizo Kanakuri, who had barely trained and struggled with sleep due to his journey to Stockholm, abandoned the race at the 16-mile mark. Disoriented and exhausted, he wandered into a garden party where he consumed orange juice for an hour before taking a boat back to Japan the following day.

In Sweden, Kanakuri’s disappearance became a subject of myth, with his name remaining on the country’s missing persons list for more than 50 years.
summary: Jonathan Liew argues that the Fury v Joshua fight is positioned where commercial potential meets a lack of jeopardy. The article opens with a historical anecdote about Japanese runner Shizo Kanakuri disappearing during the 1912 Olympic marathon.

content:

title: High-resolution global atmospheric model erases 'popcornlike' rain
content:
A new high-resolution atmospheric model developed by a team at the University of Tokyo has narrowed the standard grid spacing used in global climate and weather forecasting to just 220 meters (720 feet). This advancement contrasts with typical predictive models, which divide Earth's atmosphere into grid sections covering tens to hundreds of kilometers.

The increased resolution of the new model eliminated instances of "popcornlike" rain, a phenomenon characterized by bursts of heavy rain that appear in simulations but do not occur in real life. By removing these inaccuracies, the model provides more precise predictions of extreme local weather from a global framework.
summary: Global climate and weather forecasting use predictive models that divide Earth's atmosphere into a grid, with each section typically covering tens to hundreds of kilometers. content:
The 2026 Nobel Prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine highlighted breakthroughs that have shaped modern science and medicine. The awards recognized work that has helped develop countless drugs, enabled physicists to observe a mysterious particle, and created a tool that could act as an on‑off switch for brain cells.

In medicine, the prize was awarded for research into the mysteries of the brain. The physics prize went to Francis Halzen for his work at the South Pole on neutrinos. The chemistry prize honored research on mirror‑image molecules.

Madeleine Finlay discussed the prizes with science editor Ian Sample and correspondents Nicola Davis and Linda Geddes.
summary: This year’s Nobel prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine have celebrated work that has been used to develop countless drugs and transform modern medicine, allowed physicists to observe one of the most mysterious particles, and provided a tool that could act as an on/off switch for brain cells. title: MIT computer scientist Margaret Hamilton, Apollo 11 software pioneer, dies at 90
content:
MIT announced on Wednesday that Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died at the age of 90.  

Hamilton led the development of software for the Apollo 11 mission and was a recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom. She learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.  

She died on 30 September.
summary: Margaret Hamilton, a MIT computer scientist, led the development of the software that powered the Apollo 11 moon landing. She died on 30 September at the age of 90.

title: Industrial AI Enters New Phase with Foundation, Physical, and Agentic Models
content:
Industrial AI is entering a new phase. After decades of predictive analytics and other specialized applications, advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI are making it possible to automate more complex tasks across industrial environments.  

Unlike AI that operates purely in the digital world, industrial AI can interact directly with physical systems, enabling deeper integration into manufacturing and other industrial processes.  

These developments suggest a shift toward more autonomous and physically capable AI solutions in industry.
summary: Industrial AI is entering a new phase as advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI enable automation of more complex tasks across industrial environments. Unlike digital-only AI, industrial AI can directly interact with physical systems.

content:

title: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai Awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Asymmetric Reaction
content:
In 2026, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai for their pioneering work in asymmetric chemistry.  

Kagan and Soai designed chemical reactions that produce only one of the two mirror‑image forms of a molecule, a breakthrough in controlling molecular handedness.  

Their discovery is significant for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.
summary: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for designing chemical reactions that produce only one of the two mirror-image forms of a molecule. This discovery is significant for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.

title: CBS procedural 'Cupertino' uses tech satire to address AI and industry issues
content:
CBS’s new procedural “Cupertino,” starring Ella Stiller, Mike Colter and Rachel Keller, tackles the tech backlash through a fictionalized lens. The series opens with a tentative tone but quickly finds its footing, weaving in satirical versions of real‑world tech phenomena such as the Zizians, Polymarket, Jeff Bezos’s alleged looks‑maxxing obsession, OpenAI’s purported use of Scarlett Johansson’s voice, and debates over AI guardrails.

By framing these contemporary issues within the familiar format of broadcast television, “Cupertino” aims to capture the sense of helplessness many feel amid rapid technological change that reaches far beyond the San Francisco Bay Area. The show’s creators use the medium’s “outdated” tools to deliver a timely commentary on the evolving tech landscape. The full story appears on The Verge.
summary: The CBS show “Cupertino” stars Ella Stiller, Mike Colter and Rachel Keller. The series blends a procedural format with satirical takes on tech topics such as AI guardrails, OpenAI, Jeff Bezos, Polymarket and other contemporary issues.

title: Xbox Launches XP Division for Films, TV, and More
content:
Xbox has announced the creation of a new division called “XP,” which will focus on Xbox‑related experiences that are not video games. The division will handle films, television adaptations, consumer products, live events, and partnerships with creators and brands.

According to a blog post by Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, XP will formalize four investment areas. The first, XBOX PICTURES, is aimed at bringing Xbox worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other linear storytelling. The second, XBOX PRODUCTS, is intended to create products that are authentic to the fandom. The remaining two areas are not named in the provided text.

The information was released in a blog post by Matthew Ball, and the full story is available at The Verge.
summary: Xbox has created a new division called XP to handle non‑game Xbox experiences such as films, television, consumer products, live events, and brand partnerships. The division will bring together existing teams and formalize four investment areas, including XBOX PICTURES and XBOX PRODUCTS, as outlined by chief strategy officer Matthew Ball.
author: The Verge

title: Joe Rogan and Spotify renew $250 million podcast deal
content:
Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan, valuing the deal at approximately $250 million. The podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, remains the number one show on the platform and globally. The renewed contract permits new episodes to be released weekly on Spotify and distributed across other platforms.

This renewal expands upon the initial exclusive streaming agreement signed in 2020. In 2024, Spotify permitted the show to be distributed to additional networks, including YouTube and Apple, as part of a previous deal with Rogan.
summary: Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan for a reported value of around $250 million. The deal allows new episodes of The Joe Rogan Experience to appear on Spotify and other platforms each week.

title: Amazon Launches Alexa Tablets, New Android-Based Lineup
content:
Amazon is launching a new line of devices branded as Alexa Tablets, marking a significant departure from its previous hardware offerings. Unlike the Fire tablets that have defined the company’s market presence for the last 15 years, these new devices are designed to integrate the Alexa Plus assistant into the center of a user’s computing experience while functioning as standalone, high-quality tablets.

A key differentiator for the new lineup is its operating system, which runs full Android with support for Google Play. This allows users to access a wide range of third-party applications, a capability not previously available on Amazon’s standard tablet hardware. The devices also include preloaded Amazon applications and built-in features for quick access to Prime Video content and shopping services.
summary: Amazon is launching a new lineup of tablets called Alexa Tablets that run Android and include full Google Play support. The devices are designed to center Alexa Plus in users' computing life and provide quick access to Prime Video and Amazon shopping.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Launches $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro with Full Google Play Access
content:
Amazon has unveiled a new Android tablet, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, priced at $499. The device is part of a small group of new Android tablets announced by Amazon today, and it is positioned as a more desirable option than the company’s existing Fire lineup.

Unlike Fire tablets, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs a full version of Android and provides unrestricted access to the Google Play app store, avoiding the Amazon‑centric app ecosystem and ads that appear on Fire devices. It is available with either 8 GB or 12 GB of RAM and is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8‑core CPU.

The Verge has reported on the launch, noting the tablet’s specifications and its departure from Amazon’s typical low‑cost, Amazon‑centric tablet strategy.
summary: Amazon released a $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro that offers full Google Play access and comes with either 8GB or 12GB of RAM powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8‑core CPU. Unlike Fire tablets, it does not run a modified Android with Amazon ads.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Launches Kids Tablets with Parental Controls for Google Play
content:
Amazon has announced a new line of Kids Tablets that expand its Alexa Tablet family. The devices run Android and provide full access to the Google Play store, while adding parental controls that let parents restrict the software and content their children can access.

The Kids Tablets come in two styles of colorful cases featuring characters from Paw Patrol, Barbie, and SpongeBob. A thicker, more protective case is aimed at pre‑kindergarten children, while a thinner case is intended for kids aged six and up. title: Kenyan refugee camp workers do AI‑assisted translation gigs for uncertain low pay
content:
Refugee gig workers in Kenya are performing low‑paid tech tasks for overseas companies, often without knowing the client, purpose or payment. In a portable building at Kakuma refugee camp near Kenya’s northern border with South Sudan, a woman identified only as Grace used ChatGPT to research translations of Christian hymns in languages she does not speak.

Grace, who said she cannot work legally in Kenya, prompted the AI to translate an English hymn into an assigned East Asian language, then searched for existing versions and gathered details about the translator, author and Christian denomination. She submitted the compiled information to AOP Connect, a crowdsourced research platform owned by British AI enterprise software firm RWS.
summary: In Kakuma refugee camp near Kenya’s border with South Sudan, refugees are hired as gig workers by tech firms to translate Christian hymns using ChatGPT and submit research to AOP Connect. The workers, who cannot legally work in Kenya, receive uncertain, low pay for the tasks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: EU ends sponsorship of Disinfo2026 conference after Trump officials' request
content:
The European Union’s diplomatic service ended its sponsorship of the #Disinfo2026 conference after pressure from officials in the Trump administration, the Guardian reports.

According to the report, the Trump administration also urged Canada and Lithuania to pull their support, and both countries, along with the EU diplomatic service, subsequently withdrew their sponsorship. Days before the event, the conference’s website had its logos removed.

#Disinfo2026, organized by the Brussels‑based non‑profit EU Disinfo Lab, is scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday in a hotel in Vilnius, Lithuania. The annual gathering brings together hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers from Europe’s counter‑disinformation community.
summary: The Trump administration pressured multiple countries, leading the EU diplomatic service, Canada and Lithuania to withdraw their sponsorship of the #Disinfo2026 conference. The conference, run by the Brussels non‑profit EU Disinfo Lab, is being held Wednesday and Thursday in Vilnius with hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers attending.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Molly Russell’s father to say Instagram ‘killed’ daughter in UK cinema ad
content:

In the spot, released on Friday, Russell says “Instagram helped kill my daughter” and adds that “too little has changed” since his child’s death.

Molly Russell, 14, died by suicide in 2017 after viewing harmful content on Instagram. The ad will appear prior to the film about Mark Zuckerberg’s social media empire, linking her death to the platform’s impact.
summary: Ian Russell will appear in a 30‑second advertisement shown before UK screenings of the film The Social Reckoning. In the ad he says Instagram helped kill his 14‑year‑old daughter, Molly Russell, who died by suicide in 2017 after viewing harmful content.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Co-op Legal Services puts staff under AI call‑monitoring system
content:
Co-op Legal Services has rolled out an AI‑driven listening system that records and scores every probate‑related phone call made by its agents, prompting a whistleblower to describe the practice as “oppressive and dystopian.”  

The automated technology analyses interactions between staff and customers seeking advice on probate, wills and estates, assigning a percentage score to each call.  

The whistleblower’s comments underscore concerns that the new system places workers under continuous AI surveillance.
summary: Co-op Legal Services is using AI models to record, analyze and assign a percentage score to every probate, wills and estates phone call between agents and customers. A whistleblower described the system as oppressive and dystopian, saying it places workers under AI surveillance.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Christa Pike regains consciousness after surviving two lethal pentobarbital doses
content:
Christa Pike regained consciousness after surviving two allegedly lethal doses of pentobarbital administered during a botched execution.  

Her attorney reported that medical staff had considered Pike brain dead and were preparing to discontinue life support when she unexpectedly woke up and began speaking.
summary: Christa Pike regained consciousness after surviving two supposedly lethal doses of pentobarbital during a botched execution. Her lawyer said she had been considered brain dead and near removal from life support before she unexpectedly woke and began speaking.

title: Dry wells and shrinking water holes as drought grips Sri Lanka
content:
A prolonged drought in central Sri Lanka is leaving wells dry, according to reports. The water shortage is harming farmers’ livelihoods as they lose access to essential irrigation.

The scarcity is also forcing wildlife to gather around the few remaining water holes, which are shrinking as the drought persists.
summary: Prolonged drought in central Sri Lanka is leaving wells dry, hurting farmers’ livelihoods and pushing wildlife to crowd shrinking water holes.

title: Ethiopian drones strike Eritrean vehicles near Adigrat amid diplomatic break
content:
Ethiopian drones carried out strikes on Eritrean vehicles around the northern city of Adigrat overnight.  

Witnesses said the attacks destroyed several lorries and caused Eritrean troops to retreat from the area.  

The incident occurred days after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats and Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties.
summary: Ethiopian drone strikes hit Eritrean forces, accused of backing rebels in Tigray, around the northern city of Adigrat overnight. Witnesses reported destroyed lorries and retreating troops, days after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats and Eritrea severed ties.
